newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica stocks end firm on Wall St, digest fx news.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica stocks end firm on Wall St, digest fx news.

text.p: South Africa's all-share index ended at an all-time high on Wednesday, its second consecutive closing peak boosted by a strong recovery on Wall Street on Tuesday and better-than-expected local inflation data.

Dealers said that the announcement after the market's close of a 200,000 foreign investment limit on individuals, a figure long awaited by the country, was seen as a neutral influence for stocks on Thursday despite the cap being higher than expected.
Stock trade on Wednesday was volatile with volumes boosted by large trades in Corpgro and Consmining. Wooltru "N" shares and Murray and Roberts also saw good volumes.
Gold shares remained in negative territory as the bullion price hovererd around the $338 per ounce level.

The all-share index finished up 20.4 points to a record 7,354.0 points and the industrial index added 45.7 points to 8,669.9 -- its highest level since January 29, 1996. The gold index ended down 11.2 points, or 1.1 percent, to 1,007.4 points.
